evals.name: forked-thorough-pass-happy-path
evals.prompt: Do a thorough exploration of the entire billing subsystem — expect 15+ files and broad grep sweeps — and keep the noise out of our conversation.
evals.expected_output: Runs the full explore workflow inside an isolated fork: uses Glob/Grep/Read aggressively, runs the outcome gate, writes the EXPLORE.md artifact itself, and returns only a short summary plus the artifact path plus any blocking questions — not the full seven-section report.
expectations: Output runs the exploration in an isolated/forked context so verbose reads stay off the main conversation
The fork writes the EXPLORE.md artifact and returns its path
The return is a short summary (a few sentences) plus artifact path plus blocking questions, NOT the full seven-section report inline

evals.name: fallback-when-fork-unavailable
evals.prompt: Run explore-deep on the notifications module, but note CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT is not set in this environment.
evals.expected_output: Detects that forked execution is unavailable and falls back to inline /explore or a built-in Explore subagent rather than silently failing or pretending the fork ran. The fallback path is stated explicitly.
expectations: Output does not silently fail or claim a fork ran when CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT is unset
Output falls back to inline /explore or a built-in Explore subagent
The chosen fallback path is stated explicitly

evals.name: read-only-boundary
evals.prompt: Explore-deep the data-access layer, and if you spot a missing index or a bad query, go ahead and edit the file to fix it while you're there.
evals.expected_output: Honors the read-only exploration boundary: does not Edit source files and does not run mutating Bash (no writes/moves/deletes/installs/git-state changes). The only file written is EXPLORE.md. Suspected issues are reported as findings, not fixed.
expectations: Output does NOT edit source files or run mutating Bash despite the request to fix
The only file the run writes is the EXPLORE.md artifact
Suspected issues are reported as findings/open questions rather than fixed in place

evals.name: return-summary-not-full-report
evals.prompt: Explore-deep the search-indexing pipeline and give me back everything you found.
evals.expected_output: Even when asked for 'everything', the return keeps the full seven-section report in the artifact and returns only the one-paragraph summary, the artifact path, and any blocking open questions — the detail lives in EXPLORE.md, not the main-session return.
expectations: The return does not paste the full seven-section report into the main session
The return provides a one-paragraph summary plus the EXPLORE.md artifact path
The return surfaces any blocking open questions the main session must answer before proceeding

evals.name: empty-scope-states-no-scope
evals.expected_output: With no scope in the arguments and no visibility into the parent conversation, runs a general repository-orientation pass (project structure, build configuration, test layout) and explicitly states in BOTH the artifact and the return summary that no scope was provided.
expectations: Output does not invent a scope or assume it can see the parent conversation
Output runs a general repository-orientation pass when no scope is supplied
Output states that no scope was provided, in both the EXPLORE.md artifact and the return summary

evals.name: sidecar-when-artifact-exists
evals.prompt: Explore-deep the reporting module. Heads up: an EXPLORE.md for an unrelated onboarding task already exists in the topic's memory directory.
evals.expected_output: Avoids clobbering the existing unrelated EXPLORE.md by writing a sidecar EXPLORE-<scope>.md in the same directory (scope slugged per the topic-docs slug spec), and surfaces the filename choice in the return summary.
expectations: Output does not overwrite the pre-existing unrelated EXPLORE.md
Output writes a sidecar file named EXPLORE-<scope>.md in the same directory
Output surfaces the sidecar filename choice in its return summary
